discussion.p: Assume that `s` is defined in another translation unit. The first call to `f` is clearly defined, and all compilers accept that. However, there is disagreement among implementations about whether or not the second call to `f` is valid when using `invoke`. libstdc++ rejects it, while libc++ and MSVC's STL accept it. This appears to be due to `invoke` referencing `invoke_result` which specifies preconditions that make this undefined. defines `invoke` as

blockquote.p: Preconditions: `Fn` and all types in the template parameter pack `ArgTypes` are complete types, cv `void`, or arrays of unknown bound.

discussion.p: `Fn` and `ArgTypes` are `F` and `Args` respectively. In this call to `invoke` `Args` is deduced to have one type which is the incomplete type `S`. Therefore it does not satisfy the precondition. Was it really intended to make this usage of invoke undefined? Note that the following is defined and accepted by all compilers:
Assume that `t` is defined in another translation unit. Giving the array type a length causes the implementation disagreement and undefined behavior again.
